text.p: Top seed Michael Stich was overwhelmed 6-2 6-1 by Swede Thomas Johansson in the semifinals of the $300,000 St Petersburg Open on Saturday.
Stich looked out of sorts throughout the match and, with eight double faults and only 40 percent success on first serve, could never get his main weapon working.
The German complained to the referee during the match and again afterwards about movement of the crowd which he claimed affected his concentration.
"Johansson played better and his mood was better," said Stich. "I am not very happy."
Fifth seed Johansson, who said he was satisfied with his performance, meets Italian Renzo Furlan in Sunday's final.
Furlan, seeded seventh, had little trouble overcoming unseeded Jan Kroslak of Slovakia 6-3 6-3 in the other semifinal.
